title: Southern Serenaders in Oklahoma City: Hot Lips Page, Rushing and Walter Page
summary: The band that rescues the boys includes Hot Lips Page, Bill Owens, Walter Page, Jimmy Rushing, and young Charlie Christian.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: for him. We didn't last too long, but in order to get back we went into Oklahoma City and we met, at that time, this same band that I was talking about, the Southern Serenaders.

Now the Southern Serenaders, at that time, they had in the band Hot Lips Page, who is from Corsicana, Texas, and later moved to Dallas. I've known him practically all of my life. Hot Lips Page at that time was playing like everything Louis Armstrong ever put out, note for note. If you put one in one room and one in another you could hardly tell them apart. What a great trumpet player!

They had another saxophone player, who I grew up with, named Bill Owens, and he was playing sax and clarinet, and Walter Page, was in the band. Jimmy Rushing was the singer. And by the way, Jimmy Rushing, the only thing saved us is Jimmy Rushing's people always owned a restaurant in Oklahoma City, and he made it possible for us to eat over there, and his parents' restaurant.

And so we had to get back to Dallas, so these guys were so kind. They had a man named Simpson that played trumpet; beautiful, beautiful trumpet player. And incidentally, this is at the time that I met Charlie Christian, who was a youngster, on the guitar, and he had heard Eddie Durham and when Eddie Durham was great and he had sort of copied some of his style, plus his own ability to --
